dialogue.speech:
You browse through various volumes in the theology and religion section, but fail to find anything you don't already know.

The pantheon of gods worshipped in the Maze is a rather distant and abstract one. There are a lot of mythological tales about them bickering with each other or warring with an antagonistic race of giants, but less material offering moral or spiritual guidance.

You locate the library's small collection on Aenen. Most works are written by travellers who never reached the hidden city, merchants who traded with its emissaries, or scholars who have also clearly never been there.

There is broad agreement that Aenen is one of the oldest surviving kingdoms in the Realm, south of Ichiba, and famed for its engineering, craftsmanship and independence. Beyond that, details are sketchy. If the gnomes have written definitive histories of their own, they have never found their way onto these shelves.

Browsing the biographical section, you are slightly surprised to find, an autobiography by the General Belisarius'. It's a slim volume entitled 'The Measure of Victory'.

The Leonal commander writes tersely with the same austere confidence for which he is famous, presenting every campaign as the inevitable triumph of discipline over sentiment.

His opinions of allies, rivals and politicians are withering, while his own decisions are seldom questioned. You close the book feeling that, whether or not he was always right, Belisarius has never doubted it.

Several whole shelves are dedicated to the Chamber's official histories, annual reports and commemorative volumes. You spend some time browsing them.

They are impeccably produced and thoroughly self-congratulatory. Together they paint a picture of steady prosperity, civic responsibility and wise stewardship of Ichiba's affairs. Controversies are mentioned only in passing, troubles are attributed to unfortunate circumstances and are invariably overcome with C.o.C. foresight and coordination.

You're left with the feeling that if dissenting accounts exist, they're not shelved here.

You manage to find a weighty tome with the dry title 'The Higher Planes' in the cosmology section. It has a brief speculative chapter on a place called Dalen.
Beyond a handful of myths describing an endless forest and abundant Green magic, the author admits that little can be verified. They go on to assert that most modern scholars regard Dalen as symbolic rather than geographical, while a determined minority insists that every legend begins with a real place.

The library maintains a respectable collection on Danaos, though much of it concerns diplomacy, trade and military history rather than daily life.
Histories describe the warlike Leonals founding their city in defiance of the Maze, while more recent works dwell on disputes with the Gnomes and foreign policy.

There are plenty of reference works covering The Maze. Philosophical treatises, travellers' accounts, historical surveys, speculative theories, cosmology and theology, and so on.
While there is no shortage of material, you find nothing that you did not already know.
The Maze is your prison. The Maze moves against those who try to escape. Gates are the means of passage. Realms escalate in danger as your pass outwards. You find no hidden secrets or answers.

The cosmology section contains several treatises on the Realm of Faerie, none of which quite agree.
Some describe it as a neighbouring plane, others as a hidden kingdom that can only be reached under certain conditions. The books are filled with warnings about strange bargains, unreliable appearances and the danger of applying mortal logic to immortal beings. Frustratingly, every firm conclusion is contradicted by some other reference work.
One well-thumbed volume concludes: "Everything written about Faerie is true, false, or both. The difficulty lies in determining which before it is too late."

You browse a substantial collection of geographical, historical and political works concerning the First Realm.
Its kingdoms, peoples and trade routes are documented in great detail, though the quality of the information varies considerably compared to your recent first hand experience.

There are various cosmology, philosophy and physics references, but they turn out not be very useful to you.
However in a few books dedicated to the geography of the Second Realm, you do find some intesting information.

Beyond the civilised Domains of Danaos, Ichiba and Aenen, the dangers of the Maze close in. Inhospitable wilderness and wasteland Domains are haunted by "seven deadly spirits", and any wishing to escape from the Realm must defeat them all.
The inhabitants of the Realm founded a settlement in a flat place in the wilds - Hail Town, for a while a hub of trade routes. But they had ventured too much, and the Maze moved against them. Today Hail lies in ruins.
The traveller passing through the wilds will eventually navigate the dark Caves of Ilast and come to the restful Isle of the Gate. Below the Isle lies the tomb of the dragon Ekirth, and below that the Temple if the Great Gate, the exit to the Third Realm.

You consult several ethnographic works on the gnolls, whose authors consistently describe them as savage but indepenent and deeply loyal to their own clans.
Though often stereotyped as raiders, the more balanced accounts praise their adaptability and resilience.
Most volumes recount an ancient tradition claiming that the first gnolls were once imprisoned by a cruel tyrant who sought to break their spirits through generations of captivity. The legend ends with the clans shattering their chains and swearing that no gnoll would willingly live beneath another's yoke again.

You locate several scholarly works on the Gnomes of the Second Realm.
Though physically slight, they are universally described as hardy, resourceful and resilient. Most accounts dwell on their engineering, craftsmanship and the great underground fortress of Aenen, which has endured against the Maze for generations.
Many volumes recount the ancient legend that the gnomish race was cursed by a jealous dragon and condemned to wander the Maze for a thousand generations. Historians treat the tale with varying degrees of scepticism, but none can deny that the gnomes have survived hardships that would have destroyed many older kingdoms.

You find several references to Hail in travellers' guides and trade almanacs. The town is consistently described as a modest but prosperous settlement, known for serving merchants and travellers passing through the district.
Only one recent periodical makes mention of its destruction; a sobering reminder that even the finest libraries cannot always keep pace with the changing planes of the Maze.

Several shelves are devoted to Ichiba's history and administration. You browse civic histories, old maps, census records and collections of municipal ordinances.

Together they chart the city's growth from a modest market town to the commercial heart of the Realm, though they tend to emphasise orderly progress over colourful anecdote.

There is enough information here to satisfy a wide range of questions, but you note some interesting gaps. The Criminal Court archives are referenced, but are not open to the public. The catalogue lists several older histories as "withdrawn from circulation" with no explanation given. And while you find references to an underground sewer system and 'catacombs', no maps of such things are to be found.

You find surprisingly little. Imogen is mentioned in only a handful of works on contemporary magic.
The references describe her as an accomplished but unconventional sorceress, skilled in Black and Green magic, who has lived apart from polite society for many years. Scholars politely refer to her work as "unorthodox," while carefully avoiding any attempt to explain it.
You are left with the feeling that the information here isn't very comprehensive.

You browse through various volumes in the theology and religion section, but fail to find anything you don't already know.

The pantheon of gods worshipped in the Maze is a rather distant and abstract one. There are a lot of mythological tales about them bickering with each other or warring with an antagonistic race of giants, but less material offering moral or spiritual guidance.

You find several ethnographic and historical works concerning the Leonals, generally portraying them as a proud and disciplined people.
Their society is consistently described as valuing honour, duty and public service, producing generations of accomplished soldiers, magistrates and statesmen. Foreign authors sometimes criticise Leonal pride as arrogance, while Leonal historians dismiss such accusations as the resentment of less disciplined nations.
Leonal tradition holds that their ancestors were the last defenders of a dying world. Refusing to abandon their posts even as all hope was lost, they fought until the final gate collapsed around them. When they awoke, they found themselves in the Maze.

In the biographical section you discover an unauthorized biography of King Mnesus entitled 'The Hidden Crown'.

The anonymous author is clearly fascinated by the reclusive monarch, assembling court gossip, travellers' accounts and second-hand interviews into an somewhat speculative portrait. Mnesus emerges as fiercely proud, intelligent and intensely protective of Aenen's autonomy. 

An introductory section notes that the book has been dismissed by official gnomish historians.

There is plenty of material on the Second Realm.
This Realm is one of warring city-states. Danaos is the bastion of the Leonals of the White Order, who are constantly at war with the gnomes of Aenen, wielders of intricate machines and elemental magic. Between lies prosperous Ichiba, the City in the Crater, who welcomes all comers.
Beyond the civilised areas bounded by Danaos and Aenen, the dangers of the Maze close in. Inhospitable wilderness and wasteland Domains are haunted by "seven deadly spirits", and any wishing to escape from the Realm must defeat them all.
The inhabitants of the Realm founded a settlement in a flat place in the wilds - Hail Town, for a while a hub of trade routes. But they had ventured too much, and the Maze moved against them. Today Hail lies in ruins.
The traveller passing through the wilds will eventually navigate the dark Caves of Ilast and come to the restful Isle of the Gate. Below the Isle lies the tomb of the dragon Ekirth, and below that the Temple if the Great Gate, the exit to the Third Realm.

The library's holdings on the Third Realm are slight, but more comprehensive than any you were familiar with in the First Realm.
Most references describe the Third as a bleak and desolate world overshadowed by a vast ruined city, whose crumbling halls are said to be haunted by an ancient order of black-armoured knights. Whether these figures still serve a forgotten master or merely cling to long-abandoned oaths is unknown.
Little is said of its ordinary inhabitants, leading some scholars to speculate that the Realm itself has long since fallen into decay. The surviving accounts agree on one point: none who have travelled from the Second Realm have ever returned.

name: gnomes
friendlyGreeting: Good tidings, good trades, good tales, to you good day.
neutralGreeting: Long shadows cross our path today. Mind where your steps fall, travelers.
friendlyFarewell: Go well, friends of Aenen... may luck skip ahead of you.

dialogue.speech: Aenen stands strong and stubborn. The Maze will not conquer us.
A deal? Perhaps. We'll hear you out...
The road forgets no footsteps.
Trade winds blow through Ichiba, aye.
They call it a realm of honor. We call it a realm that forgets its own shadows.
He speaks of honor as if it were a cloak he never removes.
Where he walks, trouble walks two steps behind.
Anger is a small cloak, but you wear it bravely.
Ask them for honesty and they’ll steal the question right back.
He of many words and even more wares.
Subtlety is a language they never learned.
Gnomes of Aenen walk sideways through the world. Straight paths are for taller folk.
Mind where your steps fall, travelers.
Every corner whispers a different secret… most of them half-true.
Some fear her, some flatter her.
Even the shadows owe him favors.

They speak of honor, yes... just before they pounce. Hypocrisy makes a fine mane.
If war comes, it will be because the lions wanted applause for starting it.
Pickett counts everything: coin, favors, enemies...
If you seek purpose, look under whatever stones you dare to lift.
Half of what he sells is junk, the other half trouble.
Rumours flutter like moths. Catch one and another slips past.
Even the walls in his tavern have opinions.
No need for thanks.
Ask again tomorrow; I might be someone different by then.

name: leonals
friendlyGreeting: Blessings upon thee; thy presence is ever a welcome sight.
neutralGreeting: Move aside, stranger, lest thou hinder the Lady's own work.
friendlyFarewell: Go in the Lady's grace, friends, and return when thou hast need.
neutralFarewell: Go thy way, and may no folly follow thee.

dialogue.speech: Aenen is a den of gnomish intrigue, ever scheming, ever pressing us toward the brink of war, reckless of the consequences of their actions.
Speak thy needs plainly, and we shall see what may be bartered in honor.
Go thy way, and may no folly follow thee.
Their dealings are ever shrouded in petty scheming.

Much endureth by our shield-arm and our great fortress. 
But for our watch upon the crater's edge, this domain would have long since been swallowed whole.
Let none here forget whose vigilance holdeth the darkness at bay.
Steadfast in duty and unwavering in The Lady's light.
A villain unworthy of mercy.
Mind thy tongue, wretch, lest honour compel me to silence it.
There is no honour amongst thieves.
He is no threat, merely an irritation.
Trust them not overmuch; their loyalty shifteth with the scent of meat.

Beware their false courtesy, traveler.
Aenen's schemes have near drawn steel more times than I can count.
Blessings upon thee.
A strange crossroads, indeed, where virtue must stand guard at every hour.
A perilous sorceress, weaving powers best left untouched.
A villain unworthy of mercy.
She who tempereth justice with mercy guideth every true heart.
Leonals stand where others falter; our honor is our armor, our duty our guide.
Avarice cloudeth his judgment.
There are always shadows to be driven back in the Lady's name.
A gnoll trader of dubious repute.
Tensions rise between the realms, and many fear steel shall speak ere long.
We lodge there when duty requireth; his hospitality is humble but sound.
Thy courtesy is welcome.
We are knights of Danaos, sworn to the White Lady and unbending in our charge.

name: chamber of commerce
friendlyGreeting: Heard good things about you. Keep that up and we'll get along fine.
neutralGreeting: Slow it down, outsider. We keep order here, for everyone.
friendlyFarewell: See you around. Holler if you need backup.
neutralFarewell: We're done here. Stay out of trouble.

dialogue.speech: Not now. I'm on the clock.
We're done here. Stay out of trouble.
The Chamber runs this city. Make sure you remember it.
Talks too much about virtue for my taste.
Emmons? Yeah, there's coin on his head. Report any information to HQ.
Say that again and you'll be spitting teeth on the cobbles.
Guild scum slip through cracks, but we close those cracks fast.
If you want exotic junk, he’s your gnome.
We keep them in line easy enough. They yap and posture, then bolt when steel comes out.
Half of them are harmless, the other half are dangerous...
We keep the peace here, remember that.
Everything you see here exists because the Chamber keeps the wheels turning.
Not Chamber business, so not my problem.
Wouldn't mind the bounty myself, but he's a slippery bastard.
Good intentions don’t keep streets safe for trade. We do.
He runs the Chamber, which means he runs this city.
We're guards, not recruiters. Try the notice boards if you want busywork.
If you’re buying from Red Ear, check the goods twice.
They say the Guild’s planning something big. Not my problem unless it hits the streets.
A steady fellow, that one.
Just doing my job.
Pay my wage for the week and maybe I’ll share my life story.

name: gnolls
friendlyGreeting: Heh, I smell you from far. Is good smell today.
neutralGreeting: You no enemy... maybe. We watch you close.
friendlyFarewell: Go safe, friend-pack. We howl for your return.

dialogue.speech: Show what you bring, then we see who smiles.
Strangers go now.
Commerce-people think they own everything.
Hrrf. Too proud.
We hear he got price on head. Big price.
Hrrf. Maybe you want fight… or you just stupid.
Cowards who fear real hunt.
Try sell us shiny junk. We laugh, he leave quick.

We Gnolls strong-pack. Hunt hard, fight hard, live wild.
Gnolls no bow to city laws. Jungle give law, we follow.
Too many toys, not enough claws.
We watch you close.
Guards stare like we already bite someone.

What about her?
She a great sorceress. You be scared.
Just big sneak with fancy name.
They step in our jungle, they get lost fast.
City boss-man count coins all day.
Jungle always got things need killing. If you tough enough.
He got good nose for deals.
Hrrf. Jungle whisper plenty. You go listen.
Inn-man always listening.
Thanks mean nothing in jungle.
Gnolls born in jungle, gnolls die in jungle.

name: goblins
friendlyGreeting: No blades for these in the alleys, lads.
neutralGreeting: Fog and shadows to you, stranger. Stay tidy in the lanes.
friendlyFarewell: Catch you in the lanes later. Drinks if we both survive.
neutralFarewell: Off you trot, and mind the eyes in the brickwork.

dialogue.speech: Coin’s coin, culley. Let’s see what shines for what jangles.
Off you trot now.
Commerce boys don’t step in our alleys. Too slippery for their boots.
He’s honest… too honest. Makes my teeth itch just lookin' at him.
The Hand runs the quiet jobs… the kind you don’t brag about unless you like shallow graves.
Big words from someone so easy to cut.
If you gotta ask, you ain't deep in the lanes yet.
That shiny little diplomat's got more silver in his tongue than in his purse.
They’re loud, they’re dumb, and they bite.
I don’t mind 'em. Easy to lift from, hard to catch.
Fog and shadows to you.
You want honest work? Wrong city. You want opportunity? Welcome.
Wizards with bad attitudes make lousy neighbors.
Streets listen when he whispers.
Leonals? Pah. Big furry paladins with sticks shoved so far up they walk like statues.
Got ledgers where his heart should be.
Work’s always lurkin'. Depends how dirty you’re willin' to get your boots.
Sells good junk and bad junk... sometimes in the same sack.
Heard whispers of a fat purse wanderin' the market… and a blade followin' it.
Runs a clean taproom... too clean, if you ask me.
Yeah yeah. We're square.
Just another lane-rat tryin' to stay one step ahead of sharper blades.
